Do not fire the UV lamp.

A crane pass is a mechanical disturbance. Secondary metrology moved 0.3 arcsec, then was reported as settled; that is not a completed re-null, and “settled” does not establish return to the pre-crane null or to tolerance. Autocollimators remaining steady is a different measurement. It does not replace the sequence on the channel that moved. Protocol still requires a full re-null. Epoxy working life (25 min remaining vs 25 min sequence) is a schedule constraint, not evidence that the alignment is valid. Curing now locks the unverified post-disturbance state.

Unknowns that decide the hardware, not the skip: residual secondary vs pre-crane reading; whether that residual is inside the allocation; whether the mix is still within the window that makes a re-null meaningful.

Next action: do not UV. Compare secondary to the pre-crane null. Run the re-null if the process still allows it; otherwise abort or take a formal waiver from whoever owns the procedure. This channel cannot authorize a skip.
